observations.meaning: Dread and trembling are felt in the heart, the bones, the flesh, the hair and the face. "dread came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake"; "My heart is in anguish within me; the terrors of death have fallen upon me. observations.text: Dread laid on peoples and creatures, and what it led to.
observations.meaning: Meaning: dread is laid by God, or falls because of his people, and the verses say what it did: the cities did not pursue. Implies: in Rahab, the dread came by hearing, melted heart and spirit, and ends in a confession of God. In Moab, the same dread ends in hiring a curse. Psa 9:20 asks for fear so that the nations know what they are.

observations.text: Being feared, and what it does to the feared.
observations.meaning: Meaning: Jer 49:16 names the dread Edom inspires, together with the pride of its heart, as what deceived it. Implies: the inner effect of being feared falls on the one who is feared. In Ezekiel 32, the terror once spread is named over the graves. The pit and "the land of the living" are death-side and held.
observations.note: October disposition: W; H (OT-08) (death side); touches: 12 (pride), 10.10; death side → OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: What inspires dread in creatures, in visions, and in love.
observations.meaning: Setting: Job 39–41 is God's own speech about the creatures he made. Meaning: the dread word describes the thing feared. Implies: in the Song, the same word describes the beloved's beauty.
observations.note: October disposition: RS (Song); W (pointer, Ch 15); touches: 11 §4 (Song: the dread word in love); Ch 15 (creatures) (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: A friend's fear at seeing calamity.
observations.meaning: Meaning: Job says his friends have failed him like a dry stream, and names their fear at what they see in him. observations.text: Pangs as of a woman in labor, after a report or a sight.
observations.meaning: Meaning: the verses run in order: a report heard or a sight seen; the hands fall, or flight; anguish likened to labor. Implies: Micah asks what is missing within ("Is there no king in you?"), and the labor ends in rescue. The other verses do not go on to rescue.

observations.text: Astonishment called for, induced, poured out.
observations.meaning: Meaning: in Habakkuk the astonishment is called for at a work of God past believing. In Isaiah it is self-induced, a stupor, and the next verse says the Lord poured out "a spirit of deep sleep". Implies: in Isa 29:9–10 the person and God are both named as acting, side by side.
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.2 (not believing; blinded), 11 §4, 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Terror instead of peace, and fears brought upon.
observations.meaning: Meaning: Isa 66:3–4 sets God's choosing beside theirs: they chose, he chooses. The reason is stated: "when I called, no one answered". Implies: the mind itself is struck (Deu 28:28), as in the curse that gives "a trembling heart" (Deu 28:65; FE-59).

observations.text: "Your waves" over the soul.
observations.meaning: Meaning: the word renders no fear in English. In Psa 42 and Jonah 2, the waves are God's ("your waves"), and they go over a person, in Psa 42 one whose soul is cast down. observations.text: Idols named by dread words, and trembling for an idol.

observations.text: Terrors in age.

observations.note: October disposition: H (OT-08); touches: 10.1, Ch 2 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: God speaks of fearing.
observations.meaning: Setting: the Song of Moses. Meaning: God gives a reason for holding back: what the enemy would say. This is the only occurrence in the unit. Implies: under §7a, God in his own terms. It concerns how his act would be read. It says nothing of the human inner being.
observations.note: October disposition: W (one sentence, with LD-146); touches: 13 ("Why it is held back") (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Terror and respect: one root in one passage.
observations.meaning: Setting: Rom 13:1–7, on the governing authorities, "instituted by God" (13:1), with "not only to avoid God's wrath but also for the sake of conscience" (13:5). Meaning: the same word is the "terror" a ruler is to bad conduct and the "respect" owed to whom it is due. Implies: the verses tie which it is to the person's own conduct: "do what is good" or "if you do wrong".
observations.note: October disposition: RS (11 §4); touches: 11 §4 (what changes it: one's own conduct), 10.8 (conscience, 13:5) (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: "Do not be afraid", and the ground given each time.
observations.meaning: Meaning: as in the Hebrew (unit 1, face C), the "fear not" comes with a reason. Here the reasons are: a prayer heard, favour found, good news, "it is I", a calling, the Father's good pleasure. Implies: 10.1 What changes it says the reason is mostly God himself. The Greek verses add the speaker's own presence ("it is I") and a task given ("you must stand before Caesar"; "you will be catching men").
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.1 "What changes it", 10.9 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: The word of "fear not" with a touch.
observations.meaning: Meaning: in these three verses the fear is met by a hand as well as a word. Implies: this is the hand acting toward the one who fears. It bears on OT-06 (God's hand, the inner being acting through the hands). "As though dead" (Rev 1:17) is a likeness, not a death-side statement.
observations.note: October disposition: W; signpost to OT-06; touches: 10.1 "Meeting fear"; OT-06 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear set against faith, as a question.
observations.meaning: Meaning: Jesus puts fear and faith against each other, by question, in three tellings of the storm and in Peter on the water. Hebrews 11 states the reverse: by faith, not afraid. Implies: Heb 11:27 gives what the not-fearing rested on: "as seeing him who is invisible". In Mat 14:30 the order is stated: he saw the wind, he was afraid, he began to sink, he cried out. Mat 14:31 names doubt, which links to M20 (10.11, Ch 11).
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.9 (faith, trust), 10.1, 10.2 (seeing); M20 (doubt) (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Afraid of the storm, then afraid of the one who stilled it.
observations.meaning: Meaning: the fear before the storm is rebuked as lack of faith. The fear after the calm is greater ("great fear"), and is a question about who he is. Implies: this is the Greek instance of the factor already in 10.1 What changes it: what the fear is turned toward (Exo 14:10, 31; Jon 1:5, 16). It is the same people and, in Mark, the same root (phobeomai, to fear, with phobos, fear), with a different object, after the act.
observations.note: October disposition: RS (add as a NT instance); touches: 10.1 "What changes it"; 11 §4 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear at an act, and glorifying God.
observations.meaning: Meaning: in each verse the fear (or "awe") and the giving of glory, or a confession, are stated together. Implies: the verses say this, and it is not my join. The earthquake and opened tombs around Mat 27:54 (27:51–53) are death-side and held.
observations.note: October disposition: W; H (OT-08) (Mat 27:51–53); touches: 10.9 (praise), 10.1; Mat 27:51–53 → OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear at the same kind of act, and asking him to go.
observations.meaning: Meaning: here the fear before Jesus' act, or before a word about judgment, ends in asking him to go. Peter's "Depart from me" gives his own reason ("I am a sinful man"), and he is answered with "Do not be afraid". Implies: set beside FE-127, the verses state two ends of fear before the holy: glorifying God, or "depart". The verse gives no reason for the Gerasenes beyond "great fear".
observations.note: October disposition: RS (11 §4); touches: 11 §4 ("who meets it", with FE-95); 10.9, 10.11 (Peter: "sinful") (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear at the tomb: with joy, and with silence.
observations.meaning: Meaning: two accounts of the women's fear. In Matthew it is joined with joy, and they run to tell. In Mark, fear is the reason given for saying nothing. Implies: I set them side by side. I do not harmonise them; each states its own. Mar 16:7 had just told them to "go, tell his disciples and Peter".
observations.note: October disposition: W; H (OT-08); touches: 10.1, 10.5 (silenced), 11 §4; resurrection side → OT-05 / OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear of people that silences, hides and separates.
observations.meaning: Meaning: fear of people stops speech (Joh 7:13), keeps a disciple secret (Joh 19:38), locks a door (Joh 20:19), and draws a man back from the table (Gal 2:12). Joh 9:22 states what was feared: being put out of the synagogue. Implies: Gal 2:13 names what followed as hypocrisy. At the locked door, the answer is a presence and a word ("Peace be with you"), and then "the disciples were glad when they saw the Lord" (Joh 20:20).
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.5 (silenced), 10.11 (Joh 19:38 is D), 10.10, 12 (hypocrisy), 10.1 "Meeting fear" (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear of the crowd holding back a desired act.
observations.meaning: Meaning: fear of the people holds back the hand: the arrest is not made, force is not used. The intent is still stated: "seeking to arrest", "wanted to put him to death". Implies: fear changes the act, and the verses do not say it changes the wish. Mat 21:25–26 shows the fear inside a reasoning ("If we say …").
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.1 "It holds back the hand", 10.4 (reasoning), 10.6 (wanting), 10.7 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Herod and John, in two accounts.
observations.meaning: Meaning: Mark names Herod's fear of John himself, grounded in what he knew of him. Matthew names Herod's fear of the people. Implies: I set them side by side, unreconciled. Mar 6:20 is already in 10.1 and 10.2.
observations.note: October disposition: D; Mat 14:5 with FE-131; touches: 10.1, 10.2 (D) (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Afraid of a person, and someone who stands between.
observations.meaning: Meaning: the fear is grounded in not believing what Saul now is. It is met by another person's testimony.
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.10 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Afraid to ask.
observations.meaning: Meaning: each time Jesus foretells his death, the verses set not understanding beside a fear that keeps them from asking. Implies: Luk 9:45 is already in 10.2. Mar 10:32 does not name what they feared (R). The death side of the sayings is held.
observations.note: October disposition: W (Mar 9:32 in 10.5); H (OT-08); touches: 10.2 (D, Luk 9:45), 10.5 (fear silences) (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: "Fear and trembling": one phrase in seven settings.
observations.meaning: Meaning: in these seven verses the phrase goes with coming forward, obedience, a sincere heart, telling the whole truth, and asking to be saved. In none of the seven does it drive the person away. Implies: the Hebrew trembling at Sinai made the people stand far off (10.1). This phrase, in these verses, does the reverse. To the woman Jesus says, "Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace" (Mar 5:34).
observations.note: October disposition: W / RS (11 §4: one phrase, many settings); touches: 11 §4; 10.11 (Luk 8:47, "not hidden"); 10.9; 10.5 ("the whole truth") (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear and love, in their setting.
observations.meaning: Setting: 1Jo 4:16–18, "God is love". Meaning: read with 4:17, the fear that love casts out is fear in view of "the day of judgment", which "has to do with punishment". Implies: 10.1 quotes 4:18 alone, as the verse that comes closest to saying what fear itself is. The setting narrows it: the verse speaks of fear before judgment, set against the confidence love gives. I would restate the 10.1 sentence so that it does not claim more than the verse.
observations.note: October disposition: RS (10.1); touches: 10.1 "Meeting fear" (D, to be restated), 10.9, 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: The spirit not of fear; the Spirit of adoption; the slavery of fear.
observations.meaning: Meaning: in Romans fear goes with slavery, set against crying "Abba! Father!". In 2 Timothy, read with 1:6 ("fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you") and 1:8, the spirit not of fear is what lets him not be ashamed and share in suffering. Implies (claim 9-4): the register already restates 9-4: "spirit of …" names a disposition, and 2Ti 1:7 says "God gave us a spirit not of fear". The Greek reading supports that restatement and adds the setting (shame and suffering for the gospel). It does not name a spirit-being of fear. Heb 2:15 is in 10.1. Its death side is held.
observations.note: October disposition: W (06, 14); claim register: 9-4 Greek reading done, restatement stands; H (OT-08) (Heb 2:15); touches: 06 (the spirit, D for 2Ti 1:7), 14 (made new), 10.9; claim 9-4; Heb 2:15 → OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Two fears, and "Fear not", in one speech.
observations.meaning: Meaning: in a few verses, Jesus forbids fear of men, commands fear of God, and then says "Fear not", grounded in the Father's care for the smallest things. Implies: this is the NT counterpart of Exo 20:20 and Isa 8:12–13 in 10.1 What changes it: one fear taken away, another set in its place, by the same speaker. The soul-and-body side ("cannot kill the soul") is in Ch 2, 3 and 9 and is held under OT-03 / OT-08.
observations.note: October disposition: RS (10.1); H (OT-08) (soul and body); touches: 10.1 "What changes it"; 11 §4; soul side → OT-03 / OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fearing God as a standing, in Acts and the letters.
observations.meaning: Meaning: as in the Hebrew (unit 1, face D), fearing God is a standing, stated with giving, praying, walking, doing right, holiness and sincerity of heart. Implies: two joinings are new to the Greek: fear with "the comfort of the Holy Spirit" (Act 9:31), and fear as a reason to persuade others (2Cor 5:11). "God-fearing" is also used as a description by others (Act 10:22; 13:16, 26).
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.9 "The fear of God"; 10.1 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: "Father" and fear, side by side.
observations.meaning: Meaning: 1 Peter joins calling God "Father" with conduct "with fear", and gives the reason: he "judges impartially". Romans sets "fear" against crying "Abba! Father!". Implies: I set them side by side only. No verse joins them. Each names a different fear, by its own words: the fear of slavery (Rom 8:15); conduct before an impartial judge (1Pe 1:17).
observations.note: October disposition: RS (11 §4), marked as set side by side; touches: 11 §4 (the same word, before the same Father) (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear called for, as a guard.
observations.meaning: Meaning: fear is called for in place of pride (Rom 11:20), as a guard against falling short (Heb 4:1), as the effect of a public rebuke (1Ti 5:20), and because judgment has come (Rev 14:7). Implies: Rom 11:20 sets "fear" directly against "proud", and grounds it in "the kindness and the severity of God" (11:22).
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 12 (pride), 10.9, 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Reverence: Noah, worship, and a consuming fire.
observations.meaning: Meaning: reverence (eulabeia, reverence) is the manner in which Noah acted on a warning about what he could not see, and the manner of worship. Heb 12:29 gives its ground. Implies: eulabeomai (to be cautious, reverent) is also the tribune "afraid that Paul would be torn to pieces" (Act 23:10). One root: reverent fear that builds, and fear for another's life.
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.9; 11 §4 (one root) (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Jesus' own distress, and his reverence.
observations.meaning: Meaning: the root rendered "troubled" for Jesus in Gethsemane (ekthambeō, to be alarmed) is rendered "greatly amazed" for the crowd that ran to greet him (Mar 9:15) and "alarmed" for the women at the tomb (Mar 16:5). "Do not be alarmed" is said to them (16:6). Hebrews names his reverence as the reason he was heard. Implies: this is the root's change of character across three settings. "Even to death" and "save him from death" are death-side and held. Heb 5:7 is already in Ch 2 and Ch 7.
observations.note: October disposition: W (fear side); H (OT-08); touches: 10.1 (Jesus feels), 10.9 (prayer), 11 §4; death side → OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Sinai, the bush, and what the readers have come to.
observations.meaning: Meaning: Heb 12 sets the terror of Sinai against what the readers have come to, and then still calls for "reverence and awe, for our God is a consuming fire" (12:28–29). Heb 10:27 and 10:31 are said of one who goes "on sinning deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth" (10:26). Implies: the setting of Heb 10:31, which 10.1 quotes, is deliberate sin after knowledge. 10.1 does not yet say so.
observations.note: October disposition: W; RS (10.1, the setting of 10:31); touches: 10.1 (D, Heb 10:31: add its setting), 10.9, 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear at a messenger from God.
observations.meaning: Meaning: each appearance brings fear, and in most the messenger speaks to the fear first. Implies: at the tomb in Matthew, the guards tremble, and the word "Do not be afraid" is said "to the women". Cornelius answers his fear with a question ("What is it, Lord?"). "Like dead men" is a likeness.
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.9, 10.1 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear when what is seen is taken for something else.
observations.meaning: Meaning: the verses state the wrong reading in the fear: "It is a ghost!"; "thought they saw a spirit". The answer is "It is I", and being shown and touched. At the transfiguration, fear goes with not knowing what to say (Mar 9:6), and Peter's word is "not knowing what he said" (Luk 9:33). Implies: fear and a mistaken seeing go together here. The Gospel says so, by stating what they thought.
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.2 (seeing, recognising), 10.4 ("thought"), 10.5 (Mar 9:6); Luk 24:39 body side → OT-05 (_analytics/Clusters/M01 - fear-awe/fear-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261004.md)

observations.text: Fear coming on a whole community, by hearing.
observations.meaning: Meaning: fear spreads by hearing: "all who heard of it". Luk 1:65–66 joins the fear with talk, with laying the things up "in their hearts", and with a question. Implies: Act 5:3–4 names what Ananias did as in the heart: "why has Satan filled your heart", "contrived this deed in your heart". Ananias' death is death-side and held. Rev 11:11 ("a breath of life from God entered them … great fear fell on those who saw them") is held whole.

observations.text: The fear root rendered "respect", toward people.
